data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:12 | [2024-06-28 13:59] derbymanager : - I'm tweaking school training to be faster, hopefully it'll be better in the next days. Main squad training is working well. - Mentors have been simplified, they now give a fixed boost (the number written next to them)  to all senior and youth players in their group. The number is not divided by the number of players anymore. Each 1 is equal to 0.05 facility stars (e.g. 10 = half a star). Maximum is 30 points in a group (1.5 stars). - Slowed down form change for players. Previously they could jump almost a full step in a single day (e.g. they could go from superb to fine in only 2 days). - Board satisfaction is calculated daily based on your league position. It moves slower if you are new to the team and/or it's the beginning of the season. The baseline is 75% (you are exactly at season expectation) and better or worse position affects the baseline. For example, your expectation is to be 6th but you are 12th for the first half of the season, satisfaction will move down every day in that period. Then you get 3 wins in a row and get to 6th, it will go up a bit towards 75% but it won't be enough to completely negate the first half of the season. But if you continue to win and end up 1st at the end, by that time satisfaction should go above 75% (even though you were below the expectation in the first half of the season, the second half matters more and will probably put you somewhere above 75% in the end).

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:43 | [2024-10-28 09:43] derbymanager : I've split tactical options to better follow the engine and to allow for certain combinations that were not possible before:  - Build up type - specifies in which area of the pitch will your team try to build up their attacks. Selecting the Counters option means your team will start counters more often or, when that isn’t possible, will use the mixed approach. - Build up style - is used to shift some of the power from one build up type towards the other. Careful will move power from creativity to pressing but only if not losing, risky will do the opposite if not winning, and pressing will do it for counters only. - Passing type - specifies what kind of passes will your players prefer from long passes that favor sending the ball as far ahead as possible to short passes that do the opposite. - Passing focus - tells your players to concentrate passing towards a certain area after the action-resolution part has started (as opposed to build up type that relates to the abstract build up part) - Threat focus - sets the preferred type of shots you’d like to create, if possible.  Your teams have been set to mixed for all of those so please update.  ***Other changes***  - Experience in the scout info panel is explained better with clear indication if a player has certain aspect of experience significantly higher or lower than the others.  - Spider graph now makes no sense, I have to think what to show there now. Any suggestions? - Training is now divided into 3 categories (school is gone) and it had to be reset for all teams so please update your teams. - Since training for specific event is now too easy, training gets a penalty the higher the skill (e.g. it's easier to bump a skill from 1 to 2 than it is from 19 to 20). - Some other changes that I can't even remember anymore. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:82 | [2025-06-02 19:00] derbymanager : - You can now pay off any missing money to upgrade facilities (the limit was previously at 1M and then at 2.5M). The board will still only allow upgrades up to few levels above their target (e.g. if your facilities are at 22 and target is at 16 you maybe won't be able to pay for upgrades. - There is a new spider graph for players, always visible, so <@439665894021398539> and everyone can get a better/faster overview of opponent players. The graph gives out the average value of 3 related skills and is useful to quickly make sense of what kind of player one is.  ---  *Anyway, I'll try to explain again how facilities work. Think of them as being a bank.  1. You put money into them (effectively losing it for transfers). This happens when the investment is above 100%. 2. The money in the bank gives you revenue from interest (in our case it's better training, higher salary cap, etc...). 3. You can take the money out of the bank, losing some of the interest revenue (benefits). This happens under 100% investment.  Your board aims to keep finances stable. If you don't earn money, they won't invest. If you're earning too much, they'll invest a part of it. If you're behind too much they'll invest more, if you're close to the target they'll invest less. If you want to overinvest, you have to do it yourself by earning money and manually putting it into facilities.  Allowing you to put 10M directly into the bank instead of waiting for X weeks for that to happen effectively changes only the time variable. Financially it is the same. You also get benefits from that investment but lose cash for players. And, in the end, if you can't support that level your board will lower investment below 100% and you'll get your money back (slowly over time). It's literally like moving money from one bucket (cash) to another (facilities).  Hope that helps.*

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:95 | [2025-08-01 14:10] derbymanager : **Season 14 update**  - **Previously mentioned changes.** As announced. - **Winter break.** On 20th day of the season (This season Sunday 24.8.) there won't be any matches. Instead your players will recover conditions and injuries so you can push for more. - **Prices have been updated.** The reason is that they were basically growing exponentially, almost cubically, which worked fine for cheaper players but made top players have unreasonably different prices even though they were almost the same. To put it simply, a couple of skill points more in right places would bring 5M player to 7M, but at the top those same couple of points would make 25M player worth 35M. Buying that 35M player was a trap because he definitely wasn't almost 50% better than the 25M one... So I reduced the exponent to bring down the prices of top players. Previously the most expensive player was around 60M, now he's around 40M. Buying the best players shouldn't be so punishing anymore. I tried to keep prices similar to where they were before but that's impossible and, as always, there are those who gained value and those who lost value... - **Potential affects price.** Potential was previously a small percentage increase on player's value which didn't really make much difference, especially for cheap players. Now it's worth more in terms of price but only if it's high enough. So, the youngster with high potential could cost significantly more than a similar youngster that is near his peak. You are paying for what he could become. If he doesn't reach those heights you might even possibly (although unlikely) lose money on younger players...  I'm off to my vacation, lose my number 😅

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:131 | [2026-10-25 22:11] derbymanager : Condition issues: there are no issues. The game was showing you the injury chance, which is a combination of condition and form. But that was confusing so now it's showing condition only and exact injury chance is not visible.  Injury chance was a bit too high so I reduced it.  Changed how subs work a bit. You can set player's match status for any player (pitch or bench) like so:  Gets in: - RAT: Replaces a player in his position that has a rating 0.5 or more lower than the average of his team - CON: Replaces a player in his position that has condition below 80% - AUTO: Only gets in when he fits someone else's get out requirement (he is the right position) - DEV: Gets in only when the score is +/-2, combining rating and condition who to replace - IMP: Gets in as a priority if the team isn't winning - EMR: Only gets in on an injury  Gets out: - RAT: If he has a rating 0.5 or more lower than the average of his team or lower than 6.5 if anyone on the bench can replace him. - CON: If he has less than 80% condition if anyone on the bench can replace him - AUTO: combines rating and condition - DEV: Gets out as a prioirty when the team isn't winning. When winning he is treated as auto. - IMP: Can get out only if winning by two goals, in which case he is treated as auto. - EMR: Not a part of planned changes, only gets out on an injury  Yellow cards add a bit of weight to all of these. Subs always happen between 55-65 minutes (and a 3rd around 110 if it comes to that).  Player's training requirement behaves like this: - it goes down by 1 if he plays at least 20 minutes - it goes down by 2 if he played at least 45 minutes - it goes back to 1 no matter where it was if he played 75 minutes or more  Build up now warns you when there is an overflow of players in some area or when there are too few players in a critical area. Each warning reduces your build up.  And adjustments to the engine so defenders hold the line better, players don't tire so much from running, etc.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:7998 | [2024-06-16 10:29] derbymanager : So, since some others also pinged me about this form thing and since I want to keep things transparent but not reveal any formulas behind the game I'll try to explain it with an example.  In a formula for a single action, form is used like any other skill in a sense it has absolute value, it isn't a modifier that multiplies anything.  Unlike other skills, form is used in all actions thus it is very important. But it is also combined with FAW so you should look at all of them together.  The importance comes from being used everywhere, but how much it is important varies with your play style. For example:  There are 50 passes per match so passing will be used 50 times. Formula for passing puts more emphasis on passing than on form alone (let's say 2x) so, overall, that's 100 * passing and 50 * form. These are just arbitrary numbers for this example, they're not real numbers used in the game.  But form affects shooting as well, while passing doesn't. However, there are only 10 shots per game. Again, finishing is more important, let's say 3x so finishing * 30 and form * 10.  Total for form is 50 + 10 (+ whatever values are there for all other actions, but let's keep it simple and have only 2 actions for this example). That's, overall, less than passing (100) and more than finishing (30). But if there are 20 shots in your game and 25 passes the numbers are now 50 for passing, 60 for finishing, and 45 for form. That's why I can't give you an exact percentage, because it depends on what happens in the match.  Personally, I treat form the same as I treat Focus for example. I take it into account but I don't consider it crucial. More often than not my squad is determined simply by who is available for a specific position with the goal to increase training for younger players. Form is one of the things that helps me decide, it's not crucial.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:9651 | [2024-08-25 17:07] derbymanager : Situations that could happen with sharpness that can't happen now: - Your key player gets back from the injury before the important game. He has high condition, low sharpness... The one who replaced him has medium condition and high sharpness. Who do you play? - Your reserve DC is getting low on sharpness but your primary DC still has good condition. Do you switch them now so you have a solid replacement on your hands or do you risk not having a good replacement when you need him. - One player has medium condition and high sharpness, the other one high condition and low sharpness... The first one is in poor form and has 4 stars, the second one is in great form and has 3 stars. Which one do you pick? - Your first 11 has several players with low condition and the rest are moderate or good condition. They're all at good sharpness since you didn't rotate much. If you replace them all, the benefit is minor because of the lost sharpness, so there is no incentive to do it all at once. Better to keep 2 more players with high sharpness so you can make a few rotations every match and keep all 13 at optimal range... - You have a couple of youngsters that you want to give some training. Do you try to give them all a bit of playtime and small chance to grow, or do you force just two of them and give them more training? Right now you can't pump up training by playing more than 2 games in a row because you hit the upper limit of training effort and it'll all be gone in 3 days...

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:14939 | [2025-05-16 07:04] derbymanager : It's actually working quite close to how it is intended. It just doesn't make it easy to hyper-optimise, which is by design. We're not playing factorio. All I hear are complaints from people that want to have only 16 youngsters in their squads and play an investment brokers with their teams...  But, the idea is to have 4 groups of players: - 5 oldies, they are losing value but are at least ok backup players and provide more or less mentoring. - 5 peak players, ages 25-30, they are not growing much but bring you results. Some of them will start having mentoring points and you can decide to keep them when they turn into oldies. - 5 youngsters, these are the useful players that are still growing. They will either reach their peak and go into the group above, or they will become unhappy and want to move to a different team where they maybe can grow more. - 5 school players, they may or may not get enough playtime to train, few of them will go into the group above, the rest will get sold or released.  All complaints are that having 15 youngsters, few peak players and 0 oldies is problematic. And I think that's how it's supposed to be. You want 15 youngsters, then be ready to rotate them when they get to red training. Or get some fucking mentors. You can have different distributions of the above, like 4/10/2/4 instead of 5/5/5/5 and it should work. But I don't care that 0/20/0/0 has issues. It's your choice to go for that. The squad building part of the game is finding the ratio that works well for your team and adjusting on the fly. Not just programatically buying mentoring points for cheap, youngsters that will 100% double their price in 3 seasons (and never become unhappy), and playing the current meta formations... I will always fight against that.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part1.txt:18779 | [2025-10-20 08:08] derbymanager : Tier is just a ranking within the game. top 50 or something players are world class. Their tier is between 9.01 and 10.0 (the best one has 10, the 51st one has 9). Next 200 are elites with tier between 7.01 and 9.0... Your player is a promising youngster which means his tier is between 2.01 and 3.0.  Since it is a ranking, if he doesn't grow at all, someone else who does grow will overtake him and push him down in terms of tier. Even if he does grow, someone else might be growing faster and still overtake him.  Finally, based on his potential and where exactly within his tier he is, there is some guesswork where he might end up. If he is at 2.05 he might get to 2.95 but still stay in the same tier (since the next one is at 3.01+). Since the game doesn't know how everyone else will grow, it's really just a guess. No guarantees whatsoever. He might even grow to reach higher tier if the game's guess is wrong (which can easily be the case). But, in any case, it gives you some hint where he might end up, approximately). You can be sure he won't grow to become an elite player but somewhere around solid is reasonable.

The fact that teams are having salary issues and struggling is because teams in d4 consist of bigger teams that have dropped down and teams that have maxed out their squads so it's hard to compete with a normal squad...

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part2.txt:5878 | [2019-12-10 23:16] derbymanager : 1.) Roles. Previously, players were fixed. They played in 1-3 roles and that was it. You wanted ML to play as AML - tough luck. Now you can set him as winger and he will cover 3 wing positions. I assume the confusion comes from white and empty circles - what you see now (both white and empty) would previously correspond only to white circles in terms of proficiency (white was previously up to 10% penalty, same as empty now).  It is true that you could switch roles easier, assuming the player supported them. But this change was partially inspired by something you said salty - that tactic doesn't play part when playing against other managers as you can't predict what they will play so it's impossible to counter them. The new system should help with that as it is easier to assess what your opponent has available and how he can modify his tactic. This is the reason why it takes a couple of days to switch player's role so that your opponent couldn't surprise you.  But the main reason I made the switch is because now I can easily add new roles to players (there are currently 75 combinations compared to 40 that were before) and it should make training directly connected to what happens on the field. I'll come back to training later but I wanted to connect training with the game instead of having just some add-on that improves price no matter what you choose.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:570 | [2023-02-26 14:07] derbymanager : I did training just recently and here's how it works. Training will be calculated directly after the match is played. That means a player can only grow when he plays a game and for the position he played in. During the night update stats might drop for those who didn't play the game.  Players accumulate "training points" every day which increases their chance of getting a skill increase. When skill increase does happen, they lose appropriate amount of training points. Mechanically that just means that if the player doesn't get a skill increase today - he is more likely to get it tomorrow. But also, when he does get it, he is less likely to get it again the next day.  You'll be able to set up one of 4 trainings for the whole squad: - Physical: Improves work rate, speed and strength. These grow faster for younger players and drop faster for older ones. - Tactical: Improves marking, off the ball, positioning, and focus. These all change at moderate rate. - Mental: Improves passing, finishing, awareness, and determination. Mental skills change fast except for determination that is hard to change through training (depends on other things). - Technical: Improves handling, tackling, accuracy, technique. These grow slow but rarely drop.  There is also fitness skill that can drop due to injury and will grow first if it's too low. For example, a player at low fitness will first have to increase fitness to some normal level before he gets his other skills improved.  Determination, focus and work rate are skills that together cover all areas of play. They are used on top of any skill check in the match engine as a bonus, so keeping them high will be important. So the choice for training is to find the one that fits the best for what your team needs at the moment, but also to rotate players enough to get the most out of them, but also to balance between the skills they need and whichever one of these 3 (determination, focus and work rate) is too low for the whole team.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:6699 | [2023-06-26 14:55] randykeys : You have to offer a base minimum, which is the current market price. You can't go under it. data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:10923 | [2024-08-24 06:49] yasen_gg : - My belief is that condition is the most important stat in the game. It ties in directly with game time, training and injuries. - Condition is also very annoying - it drops fast __AND__ it drops for everyone.  The reason **I wanted condition to stop being a ME skill** is because it governed how you need to rotate to keep certain players rested in order to perform their roles. For example - playing 3x games with a BTB would have these starting values:  - 100% first game (lose 8, recover 3) - 95% second  - 90% third  Once the third game is over you are at 82%. You now need to give this player 3 games of rest to be back to 100%. Now imagine you play in a formation with 2 of those.  My suggestions were aimed at this - to stop condition from dictating the game. To stop having specific roles destroy condition and force you to rotate to avoid injuries.  I can see Derby saw an easy solution somewhere between the lines of what I wrote to solve the problems he is trying to solve. But the issue I wanted to solve was condition altogether. Why should someone be punished for playing an attacking wing back instead of a FB? Why should that player be worse for the next game because of a tactical choice?  The reason why ABAB rotation emerged is because: - Condition drops for everyone - More game time -> More chance of injuries - An injury can literally destroy your season given you barely have a top 11 to pick fights - People are split on whether training matters or even works, but the fact is - if you want to be efficient - playing 1 every 2 games was the most efficient.  I'd love to play my best team more, but I'm not rewarded for it: - Hence why I wanted match sharpness to lower injury chance - This would make me want to have my best player ready to perform on a daily basis  There are multiple other points to be made here, but I don't want to make this super long. I hope I got to put my point across.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:12823 | [2025-01-02 10:23] skuld6666 : Welcome 👍   OK here is my quick 'day 1' Derby Manager guide.....  1) You can play DM quite intuitively in a lot of ways. The usual formations work well such as 4-4-2, 4-5-1 etc. Base this on your best players available at the moment. Your first quest is to win your next game or not get beat. This is nearly always the next most important thing 🙂  2) So initially go carefully through your team and find your best 11 as a starting point. The star ratings really help there to see who is good at your current level.  3) Then you can further filter by looking at their experience level (more is always good). Then their natural fitness (if it's bad they may be a liability longer term), look at the current form, potential etc. Bad (red) form you can consider perhaps bringing in someone else for that game if there is another OK option etc.  4) A blend of younger and older players is often a good starting point - older/experienced is good for stable performances and younger for growth and to help you in future. Like in real life do you really want a talented, but unreliable 18 year old in goal?   5) Final thing for now. Look at depth in each position. You need at least 2 players that can cover each position. Your youth school can help you out in an emergency here (say you have no backup GK etc). Probably about 21-22 players is a good squad number.  6) Then look at the next opposition. Do they score a lot? Concede a lot? Or no? Do they have key players out? What formation do they generally play? Do they have an obvious star to try and stop?  Look at all these things and adjust your tactics to be a bit more defensive/attacking depending on how ambitious you think you can be and their strengths and weaknesses.  7) Then look at the players left over. How is their potential? Do they need a few games to help them train? Can you sell some who are useless and not improving? Or retire some to remove their wasted wage?

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:22644 | [2024-05-28 20:44] yasen_gg : If you have an icon - this player can be a mentor If icon is blue (ON - you can click it) - player trains slightly worse, but provides bonus to every other player (including those in the Youth School) If the icon is white (OFF) - you've decided for this player to focus on his own training and not mentor.  A thing to note - the mentorship bonus depends on this players' effort. This means that you need to make sure this player plays regularly so that he can boost the training of others more efficiently.
data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part3.txt:22645 | [2024-05-28 20:58] derbymanager : Also, mentor improves training only for players in the same group (gks/defenders/mids/forwards) across both senior and youth team.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:2733 | [2025-08-01 00:06] furysk : For tier 4 teams i'd say that a guide would be:  have 3-4 players that are Lower division completed products.  these guys will want to lead a young team more than an established player might.  Ideally, you can also find players that will be prominent in a few different formations.  For example, a strong lower division 23-26 year old that can play a defensive game will usually have a lot of use, as will a more complete central defender.  whereas a veteran fullback winger or wide forward might not get the same amount of utility overall.  Pick and choose a few guys that can grow into the mentor position at the minimum, do not sell mentors unless you have a surplus in that age group.  Be willing to lose their TL potential, you are paying for their benefit to your team by missing on a few million.  Understand what each role does in the formation in this game, some roles do things slightly different than perhaps your favorite manager would use them IRL.  the tactics test screen is a good spot to see what the impact of each role is.  Spend a little bit more on the right unpredictable youngsters that have skills where you want it.  In tier 4, those guys that are ideally 2.5 stars but occasionally 2 stars, have high potential, and have great or superb natural fitness are most ideal.  They may be slightly worse than the 3 stars in terms of counting ratings, but they'll be easier to keep happy on lower facilities/mentors which will offset some of that.  The stars are almost less important to me than the spots where the ratings are best right now, have a good chunk of 2.5 stars that are super happy, and the turnaround since they have taken over for unhappy 3.5 stars is night and day (2-4-8 W-D-L first 14, 11-2-2 last 15), although tactical decisions have helped too.  the added bonus with 2.5's is cheaper wages, which means more cash in bank for you 🙂  others can help more beyond 4 than i can, just throwing what i know for this level 🙂

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:3238 | [2025-08-27 23:29] furysk : from recent experience as someone in IV who was 7-10-20 in their first 37 and 27-6-6 in the last 39, the things that made it work for me after a while:  1) Do not build to a formation that works for someone else.  they have the players to make it work, you probably dont, so just build your team based on what you have to work with early on.  The only formations that tend not to work as easily (though still doable) are ones that aren't somewhat symmetrical.  It takes some good studying to make them work, best to not go that route until you feel like you have a good understanding.  2) Do not chase guys with high potential unless your plan is to then spin said player.  Happiness once those players hit the maximum for the level will plummet, and you'll have volatile performances.  If you can buy a player for 1-1.5M and get them to grow a lot and sell them for 4.5-5M, then fair play, but the idea of having that guy be the cornerstone of the franchise isn't feasible unless your teams growth is really significant (meaning you are in tier 1 in 4-5 seasons)  3) Look at literally any player that can help you now.  Experience is great, but if you can find the right guy that is 22-25 and is near the end of development, make them your tier 4 cornerstone and hope they accept a backup contract down the road or they can be sold to be someone elses tier 4 winning player.  I only know of your MC/FC, as i listed him this season, you have a solid False Nine and a good attacking-minded midfielder there.  iirc I even made him work at holding mid, though that wasn't the ideal setup.  I can give you some thoughts in <#1102891926371438623> for what you have i guess in brief

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:3322 | [2025-08-29 03:31] furysk : My Opinion, which is not that of an expert nor a high level player but as one who is currently making the effort to guide his team out of tier 4 to what appears to be a decent shot at working:   Sell the strongest 'ceiling' prospects that you have.  it is my strong opinion that in tier 4 and to some extent tier 3 that their happiness is too much to maintain.  Need good mentors, need good facilities, need playing time to keep playing shape up to get the most out of it.  you can offer them the 3rd, but it at some point is no longer enough.  Once you have your team going the right direction, some more high-solid/established-great/superb types (potential, ceiling, fitness) may have a better chance of being brought up alongside your club, especially if you manage to set up for a multi-promotion run which is doable from 4 to 2 but not a guarantee.  I think it's best to see what works on your own as far as the blend of things, but i would say having a good mix of starters that are best suited for fringe tier 3-4 play + some solid youngsters with skills in the right spots + 3-4 mentors is the most ideal setup on the wage budget you'll have to operate on.  Too many veterans and your wages spiral out of control, too many youths and your results get volatile.    You can make it work without selling the guys with some good $$ values on their heads right now, but that road will take a few weeks to hit positive cash flow, maybe more if you can't win some games.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part4.txt:13563 | [2024-06-13 10:03] derbymanager : So, I just checked, a player will fully learn a new role/position (it doesn't matter which) in 6-20 games assuming he gets average on random every time. In theory he could get 0 on random for all eternity and never learn, but that's highly unlikely. Whatever penalty he gets is halved in about 2-4 games already so the risk isn't that big.   Note that each role has its own knowledge level so a MC BTB might have MC HM at 0 and get the full penalty from the role. On top of that is if he isn't a MC at all.  The only limitation is that gk and outfield players can't learn each other's positions at all.  Training is reduced by how well he knows the role and only about half of it (e.g. with 0 knowledge he will still train). So teaching players a new role once or twice in their career won't stagger their development. But doing it constantly might have a significant effect.  Players also forget roles they didn't play in. The better knowledge for the role, the slower it gets forgotten. e.g. a role that's at 0.5 knowledge might disappear in a few games, but from 1.0 to 0.5 might take a whole season.

So if you can buy a 2M player and you have two options: A.) 31yo that has skills at 12 B.) 21yo that has skills at 10  Let's say that with player A you'll finish 1st and with B you'll finish 4th. In reality I doubt 1 player can make such difference but let's assume the most extreme scenario. That's a difference of maybe 500k in d4, 1M in d3... Keep in mind that we already assumed huge impact of this single player on your final position. It's not unbelievable that any extra you earn is completely negated with this one old player.  There is also boost to your reputation and possibly higher earnings later on if you get promoted, but that only matters if with that old guy you get promotion and without him you don't, which probably isn't the case for most teams.  There's also passive training boost, but that makes that player lose even more value...  On the other hand if you go with player B, there is a chance that player will earn you those 500k or 1M simply from training. Even if he stagnates, he most likely won't lose value.  In addition, player B will be better next season while player A will be worse. If in first season player B got you +3 positions on the league table, in 2nd season it'll be +1 position, and third season  B player is better.  ---  Now do the same math with 5 players and the gap becomes bigger and bigger.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part5.txt:5495 | [2025-03-17 20:10] endgamenow : The point of the table was to see how teams would perform given they maximised their potential.  Teams use money to buy players. When they buy a player, they're investing money into that player hoping they'll improve in their value (in moneyball belief, which is what I believe most people in IT4 are thinking of).  Facilities help increase the worth of said player e.g. you buy a player for 2 million, facilities increase worth of that player by 1.5 million and hey you now have a player worth 3.5 million - and then you can sell that player and gain a 1.5 million return on investment. Opportunity cost is another discussion but right now we're talking solely about player value and wanting a higher return.  As you can see, facilities have acted as a means to increase the player's value and therefore there is a direct correlation when calculating the maximum potential of a team.  As stated before, the table is designed to project the long term - "for all we know the ENLP might be more accurate the season after this one if managers don't utilise all of their resources." which is why facilities have also been counted in.

data/discord/DerbyManager/discord_DerbyManager_part6.txt:9363 | [2025-01-01 21:02] derbymanager : So, to remove any confusion, there are several things at play here:  - Every position has certain popularity assigned. It works in such way that 12th in d2 is more popular than 1st in d3 (and similarly for other divisions). However, your team doesn't automatically get the popularity for its position. Instead, every Monday the popularity moves a certain percentage towards the popularity for that position. E.g. if popularity for your position is 12 but you are at 8, on Monday it will jump to 8.6 or whatever, I don't know exactly. So, it's unlikely your popularity drops with promotion (it could happen if your team went quickly down and then back up by a big margin or some similar edge case).  - After this popularity is calculated, all teams are sorted in order from most popular to least popular and a tier is assigned to them so that there are 20 teams in top tier, 50 in the next one etc... Same is done for players, best 200 players are top tier, next 1000 are next tier etc... This is what actually affects who are you able to buy. So, depending on which teams go up or down in popularity your tier can change even if your popularity stays the same. E.g. if your popularity is 8.6 and 10 teams with popularity 8.7 go down below 8.6, you would overtake them when it comes to team tier. This shouldn't make too much of a difference though since some other teams will overtake you and you'll always be pretty close to where you should be.  - Finally, there are also end of season bonuses in popularity for final standing as well as for cup(s) if you progressed a bit so going up a division will almost certainly improve your popularity/tier. As I said, I can imagine an edge case where that's not the case, but it vast majority of cases it should improve.
